title: The $k$-th power of a $k$-th root of unity
statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i / k}$ be the primitive $k$-th root of unity in $\mathbb{C}$. Then $\omega_k^k = 1$.
hypotheses_covered: k is a nonzero (positive) natural number
replaced: The $k$-th power of the root of unity satisfies $\omega_k^k = 1$.
